Honolulu is the westernmost and southernmost major U.S. city as well as the westernmost and southernmost U.S. state capital.

Honolulu's favorable tropical climate, rich natural scenery, and extensive beaches make it a popular global destination for tourists.

Honolulu is ___E:Hawaiian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_language)___ for "sheltered harbor"  or "calm port";  the former meaning is also reflected in the ___E:related U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesian_languages)___ ___E:Māori U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C4%81ori_language)___ ___E:cognate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognate)___ toponym ___E:Whangaruru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whangaruru)___ in the tip of New Zealand's ___E:North Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Island)___ .

Evidence of the first settlement of Honolulu by the original ___E:Polynesian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynesia)___ migrants to the archipelago comes from oral histories and artifacts.

These indicate that there was a settlement where Honolulu now stands in the 11th century.  [unreliable source?] After ___E:Kamehameha I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamehameha_I)___ conquered Oʻahu in the ___E:Battle of Nuʻuanu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Nu%CA%BBuanu)___ at ___E:Nuʻuanu Pali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nu%CA%BBuanu_Pali)___ , he moved his royal court from the ___E:Island of Hawaiʻi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_(island))___ to ___E:Waikiki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikiki)___ in 1804. His court relocated in 1809 to what is now ___E:downtown Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Honolulu)___ .
The capital was moved back to ___E:Kailua-Kona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kailua-Kona,_Hawaii)___ in 1812.

In November 1794, Captain ___E:William Brown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butterworth_Squadron)___ of Great Britain was the first foreigner to sail into what is now ___E:Honolulu Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Harbor)___ .

More foreign ships followed, making the port of Honolulu a focal point for merchant ships traveling between North America and Asia. The settlement grew from a handful of homes to a city in the early 19th century after ___E:Kamehameha I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamehameha_I)___ chose it as a replacement for his residence at Waikiki in 1810.

In 1845, ___E:Kamehameha III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamehameha_III)___ moved the permanent capital of the ___E:Hawaiian Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_Kingdom)___ from ___E:Lahaina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahaina,_Hawaii)___ on ___E:Maui U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui)___ to Honolulu.

He and the kings who followed him transformed Honolulu into a modern capital, erecting buildings such as ___E:St. Andrew's Cathedral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_Church_of_Saint_Andrew_(Honolulu))___ , ___E:ʻIolani Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CA%BBIolani_Palace)___ , and ___E:Aliʻiōlani Hale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali%CA%BBi%C5%8Dlani_Hale)___ .
At the same time, Honolulu became the islands' center of commerce, with descendants of American missionaries establishing major businesses downtown.

Despite the turbulent history of the late 19th century and early 20th century—such as the ___E:overthrow of the Hawaiian monarchy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overthrow_of_the_Hawaiian_Kingdom)___ in 1893, Hawaii's annexation by the U.S. in 1898, a ___E:large fire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown,_Honolulu#Great_Honolulu_Chinatown_Fire_of_1900)___ in 1900, and the Japanese ___E:attack on Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor)___ in 1941—Honolulu remained the Hawaiian Islands' capital, largest city, and main airport and seaport.
An economic and tourism boom following statehood brought rapid economic growth to Honolulu and Hawaii.

Modern air travel brings, as of 2007 [update] , 7.6 million visitors annually to the islands, with 62.3% entering at ___E:Honolulu International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_International_Airport)___ .
Today, Honolulu is a modern city with numerous high-rise buildings, and Waikiki is the center of the tourism industry in Hawaii, with thousands of hotel rooms.

Honolulu experiences a ___E:hot semi-arid climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate)___ ( ___E:Köppen classification U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_classification)___ BSh ), with a mostly dry summer season, due to a ___E:rain shadow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_shadow)___ effect.
Despite temperatures that meet the tropical threshold of all months having a mean temperature of 64.4 °F (18.0 °C) or higher, the city receives too little precipitation to be classified as tropical.
Temperatures vary little throughout the year, with average high temperatures of 80–90 °F (27–32 °C) and average lows of 65–75 °F (18–24 °C).
Nevertheless, there are slight seasons.

The "winter" months from December to March can occasionally see lows fall below 64 °F (18 °C), whereas the "summer" from June to September can get a limited number of hot days achieving 90 °F (32 °C) or higher.

This occurs on an average of only 32 days annually,  [b] with lows in the upper 50s °F (14–15 °C) once or twice a year. The highest recorded temperature was 95 °F (35 °C) on September 19, 1994, and August 31, 2019.  The lowest recorded temperature was 52 °F (11 °C) on February 16, 1902, and January 20, 1969.
The annual average rainfall is 16.41 inches (417 millimeters),  which mainly occurs from October through early April, with very little rainfall in the summer.
However, both seasons experience a similar number of rainy days. Light showers occur in summer, while heavier rain falls during winter.
Honolulu has an average of 278 sunny days and 89.2 rainy days per year.

Although the city is in the tropics, ___E:hurricanes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane)___ are quite rare. The last recorded hurricane that hit near Honolulu was Category 4 ___E:Hurricane Iniki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Iniki)___ in 1992. ___E:Tornadoes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado)___ are also uncommon and occur about every 15 years. ___E:Waterspouts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterspout)___ off the coast are also uncommon, hitting about every five years.
Honolulu falls under the ___E:USDA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USDA)___ 12b Plant ___E:Hardiness zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardiness_zone)___ .
The average temperature of the sea ranges from 75.7 °F (24.3 °C) in March to 80.4 °F (26.9 °C) in September.

Honolulu is home to three renowned international affairs research institutions.

The ___E:Pacific Forum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Forum_CSIS)___ , one of the world's leading Asia-Pacific policy research institutes and one of the first U.S. organizations to focus exclusively on Asia, has its main office on Bishop Street in downtown Honolulu.

The ___E:Asia-Pacific Center for Security Studies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific_Center_for_Security_Studies)___ (APCSS), a ___E:U.S. Department of Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ institute, is based in ___E:Waikiki U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waikiki)___ , Honolulu. ___E:APCSS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia-Pacific_Center_for_Security_Studies)___ addresses regional and global security issues and supports the ___E:U.S. Pacific Command U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Pacific_Command)___ by developing and sustaining relationships among security practitioners and national security establishments throughout the region.

At the western end of the CDP, ___E:Daniel K. Inouye International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_K._Inouye_International_Airport)___ (HNL) is the principal aviation gateway to the state of Hawaii. ___E:Kalaeloa Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalaeloa_Airport)___ is primarily a commuter facility used by unscheduled air taxis, general aviation and transient and locally based military aircraft.

Drivers waste on average over 58 hours per year on congested roadways.

Like most major American cities, the Honolulu metropolitan area experiences heavy traffic congestion during rush hours, especially to and from the western suburbs of ___E:Kapolei U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapolei,_Hawaii)___ , ___E:ʻEwa Beach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%CA%BBEwa_Beach,_Hawaii)___ , ___E:Aiea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aiea,_Hawaii)___ , ___E:Pearl City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_City,_Hawaii)___ , ___E:Waipahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waipahu,_Hawaii)___ , and ___E:Mililani U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mililani,_Hawaii)___ .
There is a Hawaii Electric Vehicle Demonstration Project (HEVDP).

Honolulu is constructing a 20-mile (32 km) rail transit line that will connect Honolulu with cities and suburban areas near ___E:Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Harbor)___ and in the Leeward and West Oahu regions.

Approved in 2010 by public referendum, ___E:Skyline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyline_(Honolulu))___ aims to alleviate ___E:traffic congestion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traffic_congestion)___ for West Oʻahu commuters while aiding the westward expansion of the metropolitan area.  The project has been criticized for its high cost, delays, and potential environmental impacts, but the line is expected to have large ridership.

The line's first segment connects East Kapolei and Aloha Stadium and opened on June 30, 2023.   The opening of the first phase of Skyline was delayed until 2023, as HART canceled the initial bids for the first nine stations, rebid the work as three packages of three stations each, and allowed more time for construction in the hope that increased competition on smaller contracts would drive down costs;  initial bids ranged from $294.5 million to $320.8 million, far surpassing HART's budget of $184 million.

Electric street railways were operated in Honolulu by the now-defunct Honolulu Rapid Transit Company before World War II. Predecessors to the Honolulu Rapid Transit Company were the ___E:Honolulu Rapid Transit and Land Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Rapid_Transit_and_Land_Company)___ (began 1903) and Hawaiian Tramways (began 1888).

Established by former Mayor ___E:Frank F. Fasi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_F._Fasi)___ as the replacement for the Honolulu Rapid Transit Company (HRT), Honolulu's ___E:TheBus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheBus_(Honolulu))___ system was honored in 1994–95 and 2000–01 by the ___E:American Public Transportation Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Public_Transportation_Association)___ as "America's Best Transit System".
TheBus operates 107 routes serving Honolulu and most major cities and towns on Oʻahu.

TheBus comprises a fleet of 531 buses, and is run by the ___E:nonprofit corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-profit_corporation)___ Oʻahu Transit Services in conjunction with the city Department of Transportation Services.
As of 2006 [update] , Honolulu was ranked fourth for highest per-capita use of ___E:mass transit in the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_transit_in_the_United_States)___ .
The island also features TheHandi-Van,  for riders who require para-transit operations.
To be eligible for this service, riders must meet the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
TheHandi-Van has a fare of $2 and is available from 4am to 1am.
There is a 24-hour service within 3/4 of a mile of TheBus route 2  and route 40.  TheHandi-Van comprises a fleet of 160 buses.

The parantransit branch also runs Human Services Transportation Coordination (HSTCP), which mainly provides transportation for people with disabilities, older adults, and people with limited incomes, assisted by the Committee for Accessible Transportation (CAT).
Both organizations work together to provide transportation for elderly and persons with disabilities.

Since June 28, 2017, ___E:Bikeshare Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bikeshare_Hawaii&action=edit&redlink=1)___ administers the bicycle sharing program in Oʻahu while Secure Bike Share operates the Biki system.

Most Biki stations are between Chinatown/Downtown and Diamond Head, but a 2018 expansion added stations toward the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa Campus, Kapiʻolani Community College, Makiki, and Kalihi area.

According to the 2016 American Community Survey (five-year average), 56% of Urban Honolulu residents commuted to work by driving alone, 13.8% carpooled, 11.7% used public transportation, and 8.7% walked.
About 5.7% commuted by bike, taxi, motorcycle or other forms of transportation, while 4.1% worked at home.
The city of Honolulu has a high percentage of households without a motor vehicle.

In 2015, 16.6% of Honolulu households were car-free, which increased slightly to 17.2% in 2016; by comparison, the United States national average was 8.7% in 2016. Honolulu averaged 1.4 cars per household in 2016, compared to a national average of 1.8.

The ___E:Honolulu Police Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Police_Department)___ is the primary law enforcement agency for the city and county of Honolulu and serves the entire Oahu Island.
Honolulu Police Department has a mixed fleet of marked patrol cars and unmarked along with a subsidized vehicle program in place.
Marked vehicles are white with blue stripes and white lettering HONOLULU POLICE.
The Honolulu Police Departments lets officers of a certain rank purchase a private vehicle for police use. Subsidized vehicles are unmarked but have a small blue roof light.
Subsidized vehicles can be any make, model, or color, but must follow department rules and guidelines.
Honolulu Police and Hawaii County Police on the Big Island are the only departments in the state of Hawaii and the U.S. with subsidized vehicles.
Honolulu Police along with other city, county law enforcement in Hawaii uses blue lights for their vehicles.
They also keep their cruise blue lights on while on patrol.

The ___E:Honolulu Fire Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu_Fire_Department)___ provides firefighting services and first responder level emergency medical services on Oahu. Emergency medical services at higher levels are provided by the ___E:Honolulu Emergency Medical Services U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Honolulu_Emergency_Medical_Services&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .
Contrary to most other fire departments, fire trucks in Honolulu are yellow.
